notes:
Inbound SMB lead from self-serve signup. CTO (Maya Rao) reached out via contact form after noticing 429s in prod.

Background:
- Small logistics SaaS (parcel tracking, SMS+email notifications) rolled chat support assistant powered by our hosted API during Feb product launch.
- Onboarding: created org, integrated JS SDK, started using streaming chat endpoints and embeddings for ticket clustering.
- Went live with a marketing SMS->chat push 2026-03-06; observed large spikes (~60-120 rps over 2min bursts).

Problem observed (customer reported):
- Frequent 429s and dropped streams during spikes; most errors came from /v1/chat/stream returning 429s mid-response.
- Concurrency limit appears to cap simultaneous streams to ~16 from their single API key (they're seeing queueing and immediate 429s).
- Retry behavior inconsistent: some 429 responses include Retry-After, others do not. Client-side SDK retry currently uses exponential backoff but they saw duplicate messages from naive retries.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB, limited credits. They are worried auto-retries will spike token usage and cost.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need to avoid 429s during promo blasts — even short outages kill conversion."
- "Don't want to move to Dedicated yet; need hosted but more predictable burst handling."

Technical requirements / asks:
- Short-term: temporary quota/burst increase for two weeks covering promo windows, and clear guidance on recommended client retry strategy (retry-after, jitter, idempotency keys).
- Mid-term: best-practice config for concurrency limits and streaming: suggested per-key concurrency, recommended batching for high-throughput notification-to-chat flows.
- Want sample code for safe retry around streaming endpoints that avoids duplicate outputs (idempotency or dedupe token suggestions).
- Visibility: alerting/metrics in Console for 429 rate and per-key concurrency, token usage forecast.

Current status and communications:
- 2026-03-03: initial support ticket INF-2071 opened after first 429 reports. (notes attached).
- 2026-03-05: exploratory call with Avery Chen + Diego Martinez. Recorded FF-78291. CTO on call, engineer provided logs (see gmail thread).
- 2026-03-08: they pushed SMS campaign and reproduced spike; follow-up email shows 3 distinct 429 clusters at 10:12, 10:14, 10:22 PST.

Recommended actions (internal):
- Offer 2-week temporary burst/quota bump for org (increase concurrency by factor 3 or raise burst token bucket).
- Provide a short playbook for safe retry: require use of idempotency keys for non-stream responses; for streaming, recommend reconnect with resume token and client-side dedupe window. Include example JS/py snippets.
- Ask engineering to check edge cases where Retry-After omitted — ensure gateway sets header consistently for rate-limit responses. Log samples attached in INF-2071.
- Schedule 30-min technical POC on 2026-03-16 to tune limits and review live traffic patterns.

Next steps for AE/SE:
- AE (Avery): send proposal email with POC terms + two-week burst offer, include pricing impact (estimated ARR impact ~ $2k/month if they scale). Reference drive doc railbridge-poc folder.
- SE (Diego): prepare sample code + one-page jitter/backoff playbook; validate streaming resume options with runtime team.
- Schedule follow-up call with CTO Maya for week of 2026-03-15.

Misc notes: SMB, fast-moving, likely to convert if short-term outage risk mitigated. Preference to stay in Hosted API; will revisit Dedicated only if traffic grows >200 rps sustained.
